# Rapid minigames — Style Prompt

> A rapid-fire party-game film: one shouted command word, a few seconds, one action, one result. Every minigame is drawn in a completely different art medium, a fixed show stage with a host and a lives board holds them together, and the whole thing keeps getting faster.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

- A minigame is a command word, 2.5–4 s, one action and one result (a stamp, or a funny failure).
- Each minigame uses a different visual medium (two-ink print, crayon, terminal, pixel, blueprint, Swiss type, clay, cut paper). The jolt of each switch is both the joke and the beat.
- One fixed home look returns between games: a show stage with a host, a TV as the frame-within-the-frame, a lives board (or any counter), a stage badge and a trigger prop.
- It keeps accelerating: tempo, game length, dwell and command hold step up together; a SPEED UP strip wipe marks each step.
- The hero survives every medium by keeping two or three marks (a hat shape, one coloured dot, a number on the chest).

Not a style sampler reel (every game has a rule grasped in under a second and the counter connects them), not a flat game-show round with one art style, not a montage.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Home stage**: flat toon. Thick near-black outline (7 px), flat fills, one hard-edged shadow per shape (the shape in a darker shade, shifted 6–12 px down-right). Fixed furniture: marquee sign with chasing bulbs, TV cabinet, host, podium with a big button, lives board, stage badge. Behind it a slowly turning sunburst (about 7°/s) and a striped floor.
- **Each medium is a simplified re-drawing built around one trick that makes it read**:
  - two-ink: cream paper, two plates (brand colour plus a blue) printed with a 4–5 px misregistration and multiplied so overlaps go dark; halftone dots on the floor, thin blue notebook lines, big flat discs scrolling slowly behind.
  - terminal: near-black ground, amber phosphor, hand-authored glyph art (structural glyphs, an inverse block for the accent), static scanlines and a vignette, typed text.
  - others in the same family: pixel (low-res buffer scaled up, auto outline, dither), blueprint (white line weights and dimensions), Swiss (strict grid, one sans, one signal circle), clay, cut paper.
- **Hero translation**: redraw the hero from scratch in each medium, keeping the same marks. Check one still of every medium before animating.
- **Frames inside the stage**: screen media sit flat and clipped in the TV; paper media multiply over their paper.
- Draw textures once (CSS gradients, SVG patterns) and move only transforms.

## 3. Colour logic

- **The home stage takes the brand**: `--latar` is the ground and sunburst, `--latar-2` the second surface (podium, host's suit, lives board, floor lines), `--utama` the marquee, the stage pad and the host's bow tie, `--aksen` the TV cabinet, the badge, the burst behind the command word and the stamps. `--teks-di-aksen` is the badge's text, `--teks-di-utama` text on a pill.
- **Fixed to the look**: ink outline (`--tinta`), paper cream (`--kertas`), the dark TV and marquee interior (`--layar`), bulb yellow, success green and fail red (stamps and the lives board only), skin tone, spark orange.
- **Each medium brings its own palette** from its tradition (two-ink: brand colour plus blue on cream; terminal: amber on black). Do not tint a medium with the home palette beyond the one brand colour the medium allows.
- One accent follows the hero across media (a dot on the hat; an inverse glyph in the terminal) so the eye finds the hero after a switch.
- Words never sit directly on a brand colour that might be pale: text on the stage lives on ink, cream, the dark marquee, or a brand fill with its own `--teks-di-…`.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul`: Fredoka 700 (rounded, heavy; Archivo Black or Poppins 800 also fit). The command word is 230 px (190 px when long), cream with a 22 px ink stroke, a hard magenta-style drop (8 px, 14 px) from `--utama`, skewed about −7° and rotated −3.4°, with a spiky burst behind it.
- The command shrinks to a tag in the top-left corner (scale 0.3) before the first action so the result is never covered; one tag at a time.
- `--font-isi`: Fredoka 500. Marquee 66 px with an ink stroke; badge 38 px label over a 56 px number; screen headlines 60–150 px; small lines 30 px.
- Inside a medium use that medium's own type (VT323 at 46–62 px for the terminal; Press Start 2P for pixel; Space Grotesk for Swiss).

## 5. Motion quality

- **Order of a film**: open inside a game (command already on screen at 0 s), pull back out of the TV to the home stage, play a second game in another medium, wipe with the SPEED UP strips, end on the home stage holding the message on the TV for 2 s or more.
- **Slam**: the command enters at scale 1.9 and lands at 0.92 in 0.12 s (power3.in), settles to 1 in 0.08 s, holds 0.8–0.85 s, then shrinks to the tag in 0.22 s (power2.out).
- **Cuts, not fades**: games hard-cut to each other on the beat; the only transitions are the SPEED UP strips (three columns rising 0.2 s each, stagger 0.06 s, hold about 0.7 s, leaving upward in 0.24 s) and a push into the TV (pull back from 2.5× to 1× in 0.45 s, power3.out, when leaving a game; a gentle 1.1× push over 0.8 s on the closing stage).
- **The fuse is the clock**: a rope with knots, a spark that travels its length linearly over the game (3.2–3.5 s), the burnt part becoming a dashed line, a chili rocket at the end that flies off at the finish.
- **Failure is performed**: overshoot, splat, bonk or roll off; the medium's own physics makes the joke.
- Result stamps pop from scale 2.2 to 1 in 0.14 s (power3.in) at −10°.
- The host bounces 14 px on every second beat (0.14 s up, 0.16 s hold); raised arms swing ±14°.
- Typed terminal lines reveal with stepped easing, one step per character (0.28 s per line, 0.35 s between lines).
- Ending hold: nothing moves for at least 2 s.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | Expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Start inside a game, command already slamming | the rules explain themselves | an opening |
| Locked frontal home frame | the constant; only the counter changes | stage beats, the host's reaction |
| SPEED UP strips | acceleration | the step into a new round or a key figure |
| Pull back out of the game screen to the stage | scale: this was one screen on a show | the first return to the stage |
| Closing stage shot, TV carrying the message, host cheering | the show hands over to the message | an ending with contact details |
| Extreme insert on the trigger prop | the start, felt | a game or an offer starting on the downbeat |
| Lights cut to one spot, frame unchanged | stakes, the last chance | the last life, a decision |
| Instant replay (freeze, half speed, push-in, letterbox) | the joke or the win, explained | a result that must be understood |
| Split screen, two media | comparison, rivalry | two options, before and after |

## 7. Native moves

- **Style switch per game.** Each task is drawn in the medium that suits it. *Fits content like:* the steps of a recipe (batter in two-ink, ingredients in a terminal, the finish in woodcut); a nurse's day; a class's three exercises.
- **Command word.** One verb is script, subtitle and downbeat. *Fits content like:* FLIP! at a food stall; SCAN! at a checkout; BREATHE! in a yoga class; SIGN! at a contract signing.
- **Counter as a loyalty card or lives board.** Slots fill or crack without narration. *Fits content like:* a stamp card; retries on a driving test; chances left on a quiz.
- **SPEED UP.** Everything steps up together. *Fits content like:* rush hour; the last week before a deadline; a kitchen during dinner service.
- **Failure becomes the solution.** Material from an earlier failure returns as the answer. *Fits content like:* a burnt batch that becomes the signature flavour; a bug that becomes a feature; a missed train that leads to the right meeting.
- **The TV carries the last word.** The closing stage holds the message big on the screen. *Fits content like:* a weekend promo with a phone number; a channel's next episode; a class's sign-up link.

## 8. Pitfalls

- A luminance-ramp ASCII figure is mush: hand-author the glyphs and use an inverse block for the accent.
- A failure at high tempo goes unread: make the action overshoot and hit something, or replay it.
- Command tags pile up: one tag at a time; later commands replace it.
- A 100 % white flash reads as a blank frame: cap flashes near 60 %.
- Do not tint a medium with the home palette, and do not give two games the same medium back to back.
- Do not put text on the brand colour without its `--teks-di-…` token: pale brands vanish.
- Keep the games short: a game that needs explaining is a scene, not a minigame.

# Rapid minigames: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.6, medium 2.6, long 3.8.

## hook

- en: open inside a terminal minigame, the command word already slamming big on its burst, then a corner tag; typed lines, fuse burning
- id: buka di dalam gim terminal, kata perintah sudah membentak besar di bintang lalu jadi tag di pojok; glif dan baris diketik, sumbu terbakar

## problem

- en: a game fails on purpose: the action overshoots and splats, a life cracks off the board, the fuse keeps burning
- id: satu gim gagal dengan sengaja: aksinya kebablasan dan pecah, satu nyawa retak lepas dari papan, sumbu terus terbakar

## fact

- en: pull back out of the game screen to the home stage: the TV replays the game, an OK stamp lands and a loyalty slot fills
- id: mundur keluar dari layar gim ke panggung rumah: TV memutar ulang gim, cap OK mendarat dan satu slot kartu setia terisi

## step

- en: a new minigame in another medium (two-ink print): the command slams big on a yellow starburst, shrinks to a tag, one action, one stamp
- id: gim baru dalam gaya lain (cetak two-ink): perintah membentak besar di bintang kuning, mengecil jadi tag, satu aksi, satu cap

## compare

- en: split screen, two media side by side playing the same command; the faster one gets the stamp
- id: layar terbelah, dua gaya gambar berdampingan memainkan perintah yang sama; yang lebih cepat dapat cap

## number

- en: SPEED UP strips rise over the frame, then the home stage with the key figure slammed onto the TV screen
- id: strip NGEBUT naik menutup layar, lalu panggung rumah dengan angka kunci menghantam layar TV

## proof

- en: instant replay of the winning action: freeze, half speed, push-in, a caption in the medium's own type
- id: tayang ulang aksi yang berhasil: beku, setengah kecepatan, kamera maju, keterangan dalam huruf gaya itu

## offer

- en: the trigger prop in extreme close-up, the button pressed on the downbeat, the offer slams onto the TV as the new command
- id: properti pemicu dari dekat, tombol ditekan tepat di ketukan, penawaran menghantam layar TV sebagai perintah baru

## cta

- en: after the strips, the home stage: the TV shows the name and contact big, the host cheers, the loyalty card fills; held 2 s
- id: setelah strip, panggung rumah: TV memajang nama dan kontak besar, pembawa acara bersorak, kartu setia penuh; diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the home stage locked frontal, every life kept, host cheering; a high-score card stays up; held 2 s
- id: panggung rumah terkunci menghadap depan, semua nyawa utuh, pembawa acara bersorak; kartu skor tinggi bertahan; diam 2 detik

      /* Terminal: amber di atas hitam, garis pindai statis. */

      .rays { position: absolute; left: -240px; top: -660px; width: 2400px; height: 2400px; background: repeating-conic-gradient(var(--latar-2) 0 6.43deg, transparent 0 12.86deg); opacity: 0.55; }

            .pill { padding: 4px 30px 8px; border-radius: 44px; background: var(--utama); color: var(--teks-di-utama); border: 7px solid var(--tinta); font: 700 66px/1.1 var(--font-judul); }

  <body>
    <div id="root" data-composition-id="main" data-start="0" data-duration="15" data-width="1920" data-height="1080" data-fps="30">
      <!-- Adegan 1, pembuka: gim terminal, TAKAR! sudah membentak di detik 0. -->
      <div class="sc" id="s1" data-role="hook"></div>
      <!-- Adegan 2, fakta: panggung rumah, TV memutar gim tadi, cap OK. -->
      <div class="sc" id="s2" data-role="fact"></div>
      <!-- Adegan 3, langkah: gim duo, FLIP! besar di tengah lalu jadi tag. -->
      <div class="sc" id="s3" data-role="step"></div>
      <!-- Adegan 4, penutup: strip NGEBUT!, lalu panggung dengan kontak besar di TV, diam 2 detik lebih. -->
      <div class="sc" id="s4" data-role="cta"></div>
    </div>
    <script>
      const PI = Math.PI, cos = Math.cos, sin = Math.sin;
      const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
      const rnd = ((s) => () => ((s = (s + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0), ((((s ^ (s >>> 15)) * (s | 1)) >>> 0) % 1000) / 1000))(7);
      const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s);
      // Bentuk bertepi tinta dengan bayangan keras di kanan-bawah.
      const part = (shape, fill, sh = 8) =>
        `<g style="fill:color-mix(in oklab, ${fill} 66%, black);transform:translate(${sh}px,${sh}px)">${shape}</g><g style="fill:${fill};stroke:var(--tinta);stroke-width:7;stroke-linejoin:round">${shape}</g>`;
      const rr = (x, y, w, h, r) => `<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${r}"/>`;
      const ci = (x, y, r, f) => `<circle cx="${x}" cy="${y}" r="${r}"${f ? ` style="fill:${f}"` : ""}/>`;
      const star = (n, R, r) => Array.from({ length: n * 2 }, (_, i) => `${((i % 2 ? r : R) * cos((i * PI) / n - PI / 2)).toFixed(1)},${((i % 2 ? r : R) * sin((i * PI) / n - PI / 2)).toFixed(1)}`).join(" ");
      // Kata perintah dan cap hasil.
      const cmdHtml = (id, word) => {
        const w = word.length * 95 + 240;
        return `<div class="cmd" id="${id}"><svg width="${w}" height="440" viewBox="${-w / 2} -220 ${w} 440"><polygon points="${star(28, w / 2, w * 0.4).replace(/(-?[\d.]+),(-?[\d.]+)/g, (_, a, b) => `${a},${b * 0.55}`)}"/></svg><b>${word}</b></div>`;
      };
      const cmd = (id, t0, hold, slam) => {
        const e = "#" + id, n = $(e + " b").textContent.length;
        if (slam) tl.fromTo(e, { scale: 1.9 }, { scale: 0.92, duration: 0.12, ease: "power3.in" }, t0).to(e, { scale: 1, duration: 0.08 }, t0 + 0.12);
        else tl.to(e, { scale: 1.07, duration: 0.1, yoyo: true, repeat: 1 }, t0 + 0.25);
        tl.to(e, { x: 60 + n * 20, y: 100, scale: 0.3, duration: 0.22, ease: "power2.out" }, t0 + hold);
        tl.to(e + " svg", { opacity: 0, duration: 0.15 }, t0 + hold);
      };
      const stamp = (id, t) => tl.set("#" + id, { autoAlpha: 1 }, t).fromTo("#" + id, { scale: 2.2, rotation: 0 }, { scale: 1, rotation: -10, duration: 0.14, ease: "power3.in" }, t);
      const stpHtml = (id, x, y) => `<div class="stp" id="${id}" style="left:${x}px;top:${y}px">OK!</div>`;
      // Sumbu waktu: percikan jalan sepanjang tali, tali terbakar jadi garis putus-putus.
      const fuseHtml = (id) => {
        const rays = Array.from({ length: 9 }, (_, i) => `<line x1="45" y1="45" x2="${45 + 34 * cos(i * 0.7)}" y2="${45 + 34 * sin(i * 0.7)}" style="stroke:${i % 3 ? "var(--lampu)" : "var(--kertas)"};stroke-width:4;stroke-linecap:round"/>`).join("");
        const knots = [1, 2, 3].map((i) => `<i class="knot" style="left:${i * 25}%"></i>`).join("");
        return `<div class="fuse" id="${id}"><i class="char"></i><i class="rope"></i>${knots}<i class="spark"><svg width="90" height="90">${rays}<circle cx="45" cy="45" r="11" style="fill:var(--lampu)"/><circle cx="45" cy="45" r="5.5" style="fill:var(--api)"/></svg></i>
          <svg class="chili" width="70" height="100" viewBox="-35 -60 70 100"><g transform="rotate(-18)">${part(`<path d="M-14 -34 Q0 -48 14 -34 L18 22 Q0 40 -18 22 Z"/>`, "var(--gagal)", 5)}${part(`<path d="M-8 -36 Q0 -58 14 -50 Q4 -46 8 -36 Z"/>`, "var(--sukses)", 4)}</g></svg></div>`;
      };
      const fuse = (id, t0, dur) => {
        const e = "#" + id + " ";
        tl.fromTo(e + ".rope", { scaleX: 1 }, { scaleX: 0, duration: dur, ease: "none" }, t0);
        tl.fromTo(e + ".char", { scaleX: 0 }, { scaleX: 1, duration: dur, ease: "none" }, t0);
